request: Analyze GSE233485 for PMID 37639610 (Impaired age-associated mitochondrial translation is mitigated by exercise and PGC-1alpha.): how exercise affects gene expression as the paper intends.

final.assay: bulk RNA-seq (TruSeq v2, HiSeq 2500 single-end, salmon v1.1.0, GRCm38) of gastrocnemius muscle (S3.6.p1, FIG1)
final.samples: WT, PGC-1a mKO and PGC-1a mTG male mice at 3 mo and 24 mo; n = 6 per group except mKO 3 mo n = 5 (FIG1 legend)
final.primary_estimand: For GSE233485: age (24 vs 3 mo) and PGC-1a loss/gain-of-function effects on muscle transcription (S1.1.p1). The paper's exercise evidence is NOT in this series: exercise effects come from proteomics (wheel-running cohorts from ref 21, FIG4C; treadmill-trained vs sedentary 25 mo mice, TMT16plex, MassIVE MSV000092099, FIG4D, S3.15) and the RNA-seq is used only to show that mTG mimics the exercise pattern in the sedentary state (S1.4.p1, SI Fig S3H).
planned_contrasts: WT 24 mo vs WT 3 mo (aging; S1.1.p1, FIG1E FDR<0.05 markers; no DEG count reported)
mKO vs WT and mTG vs WT within age (PGC-1a dependence; S1.1.p1)
No exercise contrast exists in GSE233485 (exercise = proteomics, FIG4C/D, S3.2, S3.15, DA.p1)
final.paper_method: edgeR on the count matrix, genes with >= 1 CPM in all 5-6 replicates (S3.7.p1; GEO data_processing); PCA/z-score clustering on log2 TPM (S3.8.p1)
final.paper_results: 860 genes aligned with PC1/PC2; cluster 1 of mitochondrial genes; top GO terms include translation (S1.1.p1). No exercise DEG list from RNA-seq.

paper_reconstruction.reasoning: S0.p2 and S1.1.p1 describe the RNA-seq as young/old x WT/mKO/mTG. S1.4.p1 and the FIG4 legend: exercise results are proteomic (ref 21 data for wheel running; own TMT proteomics for treadmill in 25 mo mice, limma empirical Bayes). DA.p1 deposits RNA-seq in GSE233485 and proteomics in MassIVE MSV000092099. FDR < 0.01 (S3.7.p1) applies to the RNA-seq edgeR analysis; the FIG1 legend marks genes at FDR < 0.05.

checks: DA.p1 names GSE233485 as the paper's RNA-seq deposit
GEO series: 35 gastrocnemius samples, WT/mKO/mTG x 3/24 mo, male, salmon GRCm38 release 100, matching S3.6.p1 and FIG1 (n=6, mKO 3 mo n=5)
Matrix GSE233485_WT_mKO_mTG_3-24mo_Count_Matrix_TPM.tsv.gz: 35 columns whose group prefixes match the GEO group counts exactly
The metadata input is a sample sheet derived from the matrix column names (prep_metadata.py) because the GEO records do not carry the animal IDs used as matrix column names

ownership.reasoning: Series, tissue, design and n match the paper; the only deposited matrix is the TPM file.

final.mapping_level: group (genotype x age) from matrix column prefixes; GSM-level mapping not determinable

candidates.value: align matrix columns to GSM ids via GEO description (WT_3mo_1 ...)
candidates.reason_rejected: matrix columns are animal IDs (MCK_3874, MKO_SO_23) absent from every GEO field; matching rep numbers would be position-based

alignment.reasoning: The matrix columns encode genotype and age in their prefixes (MCK = muscle creatine kinase promoter PGC-1a transgene = mTG; MKO = muscle knockout; _SO / WSO = old). prep_metadata.py decodes them and verifies that the six group sizes equal the GEO counts (6/6/5/6/6/6; the unique n=5 group is mKO 3 mo, as in FIG1). Group labels are therefore reliable; individual GSM ids are not assigned.

final.paper_input: edgeR on salmon counts (S3.7.p1); counts are not deposited, only TPM
final.evidence: every column sums to 1e6; non-zero values are non-integer (0.016% integers); 60.7% zeros explain the 0.607 integer fraction; file name and data_processing state TPM

matrix.reasoning: Column sums are 1e6 and data_processing says the count matrix is comprised of TPM values. The paper's edgeR route would need counts, which are not deposited.

final.available_factors: genotype (WT/mKO/mTG) x age (3/24 mo), all sedentary

design.stop_reason: GSE233485 contains no exercised animals: all 35 samples are sedentary WT/PGC-1a mKO/mTG mice at 3 or 24 mo. The paper's exercise effects are proteomic (wheel running, ref 21; treadmill 25 mo, MassIVE MSV000092099; FIG4C/D, S1.4.p1). An mTG-vs-WT or age contrast is a genetic or aging estimand and must not be reported as an exercise effect.

candidates.value: mTG vs WT as an exercise proxy (S1.4.p1, SI Fig S3H)
candidates.reason_rejected: PGC-1a overexpression is a genetic model, not exercise; the paper itself only uses it as a sedentary-state comparison

design.reasoning: S0.p2, S1.1.p1 and FIG1: the RNA-seq design is age x genotype. S3.2 describes the exercise cohorts, which were profiled by proteomics (S3.15, FIG4C/D legend). The request asks for exercise effects on gene expression; this series cannot identify that estimand.

discrepancies.paper: exercise effects measured by proteomics (FIG4C/D; MassIVE MSV000092099; ref 21)
discrepancies.data: GSE233485 holds only sedentary genotype x age RNA-seq
matrix uses animal IDs not present in GEO records; groups decodable from prefixes, GSM mapping not
